label: PF Backlog 537
title: Epic-scoped work selection + epic execution-order view (scheduler + API + CLI)
body:
## Why
The scheduler could answer "what can run now?" for the whole backlog and for task-contracts, but not
**scoped to an epic**. The data (epic children, eligibility, dependency graph, priority) already supported
it, so this exposes two read-only views.

## What
- Epic-scoped selection: `scheduler.eligible_backlog(..., epic=)` / `scheduler.next_eligible(..., epic=)`
  return the top eligible child of an epic (deps still resolve against the full backlog).
- Epic execution-order view: `scheduler.epic_order(scope, project, epic)` - an epic's OPEN children ordered
  by dependency wave -> priority, each with READY/wait + blocking reasons.

## Where (surfaces)
- API: `GET /engineering/schedule/eligible?epic=` and `/schedule/next?epic=`; `GET /backlog/epics/{id}/order`.
- CLI: `/wg schedule eligible|next|status --epic ID`; `/pf backlog epic-order <id>`.

## How verified
- Unit: test-framework/tests/pipeline/test_scheduler_eligibility.py (epic filter + wave ordering).
- Gates: scheduler_check, api_contract_check, pf_surface_check, wg_surface_check, wired_audit.
- Live: next_eligible(epic=BI-PF-0390) -> BI-PF-0393; epic-order matches the intended wave plan.

## Notes
Identifier is the epic **ID** (e.g. BI-PF-0390), not its title. Selection is read-only (no new store/writer).
The claim/work surface (/wg work) is a follow-up.
